session.verified: signedOut: verified 2026-09-07 on the live web player - the Sign In control matched after the service dropped the session, the standing watch posted it and the App's status flipped to needs-attention (evidence probe); signedIn: the account/user menu that replaces it, not yet seen by the watch 2026-09-18: the page's chrome is a late and flaky witness - after the 08:43 boot the home page showed its Sign In control for five minutes while MusicKit held the user token throughout (signed-out at 08:43:20 and :24, signed-in only at 08:48:19 once playback began; the wall wrote needs-attention in between). Now the adapter's context script (a music slice carries no page script of its own) writes MusicKit's own word on the document root (data-prism-mk-auth = 1 while isAuthorized and a Music-User-Token are there, 0 when MusicKit says not, absent until MusicKit is up), kept current by authorizationStatusDidChange / userTokenDidChange and a poll (1 s for the first 30 s, then 10 s). signedIn reads the mark first; the Sign In controls count only under html[data-prism-mk-auth=0] (MusicKit up and saying not authorised) - before MusicKit has spoken they count for nothing, so a boot no longer posts a signed-out and recycles the page (two signed-outs and a signed-in 1.5 s later were seen at the 08:57 boot with the weaker scoping); the idmsa.apple.com link alone counts while the mark is not 1 (a sign-in page carries no MusicKit). The token itself lives in the page's own storage, which Prism never wipes (spec 10).

notes: §32 music adapter slice. Apple Music has no ads on any tier, so there is no ad-break signal by design (audio intermission never engages). Play / pause are deliberately not declared: amp-playback-controls-play is a single toggle, so a human's play/pause forwards through MusicKit's own Media Session handlers in core (the same functions the OS media keys run). Playback needs an Apple ID with a subscription. Play orders (2026-09-17, spec 32 layer 5): the service's shuffle through MusicKit's shuffleMode (musicShuffle); Prism's true shuffle and reverse through the track list (musicTracks) and a song-id queue (musicQueue). Session (2026-09-18): MusicKit's authorisation is the evidence for signed in; the page's Sign In control counts only while MusicKit is not authorised.
